text.text: The Philips Videopac was a cartridge-based home video game console introduced in Europe in 1978 as the regional counterpart to the Magnavox Odyssey². Designed by Ralph H. Baer, it combined a programmable game console with a built-in membrane keyboard, allowing games to incorporate educational and computer-like features uncommon at the time. Powered by an Intel 8048 microcontroller and custom Intel graphics hardware, the Videopac offered a library of more than 60 officially released cartridges, including titles such as KC Munchkin!, Smithereens!, and Quest for the Rings. While the Odyssey² name was used in North America, the Videopac brand became popular throughout Europe and Brazil, earning a dedicated following thanks to its unique gameplay, educational software, and distinctive hardware design.
